decision: Pre-index boundary edits require refreshed encoder inputs, identities, ownership, index statistics and rankings. A fixed-domain post-retrieval local intervention is a distinct research setting and must be specified before new utility supervision; no new method gain established.
index_findings: Unchanged raw leaf text and leaf_id do not imply unchanged dense encoder input: the input also includes inherited path and the current owner chunk anchor. Boundary edits can change both.

Even if every leaf vector and leaf hit is deliberately held fixed, leaf-to-owner aggregation changes the candidate partition, candidate text, support count, maximum score and reciprocal-rank accumulation.
Chunk IDs are ordinal identifiers rather than content/span/version identities. A split can change downstream unchanged chunks IDs, while an old ID can refer to changed text.

The existing full-build route recomputes enrichment and all three indexes. Conditional vector reuse is a proposed safe optimization contract, not an implemented incremental cache or an observed speedup.

index_source_evidence.fact: Gap cuts deterministically define contiguous atom spans; a split/merge changes grouping, not the atom sequence.
Legacy chunk rendering strips and joins atoms then collapses whitespace. This differs from exact source rendering.
Each new chunk inherits path/depth/parent_id from maximum atom-overlap seed unit; strict > update means ties retain the first listed seed span.
New chunk text is normalized atom join or source_view.render; chunk_id/chunk_index are output ordinals and prev/next IDs are regenerated. Source mode stores exact source geometry.
Leaf id/index/own text are based on global atom index; owner_chunk_id/chunk_index/path/depth/parent_id and source boundary metadata come from the new chunk.
Source snapshots are captured before enrichment mutates record.text.
Persisted source snapshot includes text hash/source-document hash/coordinate/geometry; leaf snapshot also binds owner and chunk index.
Reload validates current IDs/geometry/owner against saved snapshot and accepts only raw or exact normalized source text; editing ownership while reusing stale snapshot is invalid.
Retrieval text normalization applies NFKC, CRLF normalization, whitespace/blank-line collapse and strips exterior whitespace.
Chunk number signature depends on text then path; anchor combines number signature, first line and path; enrichment overwrites these fields and normalized text.
Leaf enrichment records current owner anchor; own path/signature/title/anchor fields may change although raw leaf body stays fixed. token_est is filled only if missing.
All chunks are enriched first; leaves are then enriched against current owner lookup.
Actual leaf dense string = path_text + current owner anchor or number signature/fallback + leaf text, with [SEP] separators; current id_map uses leaf IDs.
Chunk dense string = path + number signature + anchor + chunk text; vectors and ordinal id_map are built together.
Encoder tokenizes the composed strings with truncation=True (default max_length512), attention-mask mean pooling and optional L2 normalization (defaultTrue); no content-addressed cache here.
IndexFlatIP stores float32 vectors by positional index; id_map.npy separately maps rows to object IDs.
Search encodes query, searches current index, maps row positions to IDs, ranks and filters/merges query variants. A reusable individual vector does not freeze global top-k.
Leaf hits map through leaf.owner_chunk_id to current chunk text/metadata; unique support_leaf_ids define hit_count and max leaf scores.
Chunk and anchor routes are merged into the new chunk candidate; leaf anchor hits also map through current owner.
RRF sums each leaf rank contribution under current owner, combines chunk/anchor ranks and uses chunk_id as a final tie key.
Adjacency/children/prev/next and combined chunk+leaf anchor lookup depend on regenerated chunk records.
Lexical documents include path/signature/anchor/normalized text; chunk+leaf corpus recomputes document frequency, total documents and average length.
BM25 uses global N, document frequency and avgdl, so changing chunks can change scores for otherwise unchanged leaf anchor documents.

Entry validates inputs, enriches all records, regenerates lookups/adjacency/anchors then builds leaf/chunk dense and BM25 indexes. metadata_only returns before model/index construction; it does not refresh numeric indexes.
Current lookup aggregation and fusion feed tree expansion and local branch retrieval; updated candidate relationships propagate further.
Refiner atom encoding consumes atom texts with normalize=False; this representation is not automatically the enriched retrieval embedding.

Refiner document encoding depends on atom embeddings/mask, while heads also consume current g0 positions. A boundary change need not require atom reencoding under an identical model contract, but edit-head outputs must be recomputed if g0 changes.

next_step: Specify the minimal post-retrieval intervention with stable source identities and explicit distinctions among metadata-only, passage-changing and output-invariant edits. Do not restart the closed packing variants on the same two natural questions.

findings.statement: all_candidates is exported to reranker_input independently of retrieval packed_evidence. The retrieval pack is not necessarily a serial gate before reranking.

The BGE pair consists of normalized query_text and passage_text. Explicit passage_text overrides reconstruction; otherwise number_signature, path_text and text are newline-joined. IDs are not direct BGE pair text, but affect deduplication and tie-breaking.

Splitting or merging changes BGE input when the effective selected pair passages change; whitespace normalization, explicit unchanged passage_text, candidate exclusion or token truncation can mask a raw-text edit. A changed raw record alone is not proof of a changed encoded input.

Default retrieval/reranker adapters read provided artifacts or existing run-directory files. Runner commands are attempted only when no resolved artifact path is present. Integration prefers reranker pack_bridge, then reranked_candidates, before retrieval fallbacks. An upstream edit with old preferred downstream artifacts can leave the actual request unchanged.

Inspected production retrieval pack, reranker pack_bridge and integration select_evidence select existing whole evidence records; they do not merge touching source intervals. Their item limits count records. Legacy budgets sum per-item estimates; opt-in integration pack_cost instead measures the whole actual evidence block.

The research selector merges only touching selected disjoint intervals, refuses overlaps, does not fill gaps, caps merged runs at three and measures the fully rendered proposed runs. Its generated span IDs and per-run evidence records differ from production chunk records. Atomic scores rank candidates; the merged output run is not a newly scored candidate.

Actual generation evidence renders doc/chunk/query IDs, ranks, six-decimal rerank score, role, hit_type, source_views, path_text, token_est and expansion_depth, followed by passage_text. Therefore unchanged body does not imply unchanged model-visible request. Unused arbitrary meta fields are not directly serialized by this renderer, though designated metadata can affect ordering, restoration or validation.

request_compiler appends render_evidence_block output to final user messages, and LLMService sends the compiled payload. Legacy integration preview has a different template and must not be treated as the actual block; source-mode preview delegates to the actual renderer.

Opt-in source restoration overrides evidence passage with validated source snapshot text while retaining ranking semantics and recording source_text_changed. This can change generation input without recomputing retrieval or reranker scores.

build_scored_records checks record/score counts and zips scores onto current records; it is not a content-bound cache validator. Valid reuse requires binding the effective query/passage encoding and model/tokenizer/truncation/runtime specification. Parent/child overlap, identical IDs, source coverage or unchanged raw query alone does not establish this. Held scores are permissible only as an explicitly fixed-score control.

The older JEV client cache key binds endpoint, complete payload and prompt_version, including task IDs, batch state, choice criteria and model/provider fields. The conditional core separately binds arm, model/version/counter/limits and payload hash. Matching query and unit text alone does not reproduce either key after changing IDs, pack, criterion, batch or bound settings.

assertions: Split and coalesced contain exactly the same source character union, but have two versus one BGE query-passage pairs and different actual compiled evidence messages.
Production select_evidence keeps two records under an ample item/byte budget; it does not perform the research coalescing.
The unused meta-only variant leaves the actual compiled messages unchanged.
Any changed chunk ID is rendered and therefore cannot be called a model-invisible metadata edit.

packing_audit.research_boundary: A propagated split/merge and fresh content-bound scoring can test a changed model input. Wiring, source coverage and input changes alone do not establish utility, quality, causality of learned boundaries or novelty. Evidence-block budgeting is not a bound on the full system/query/memory/provider message payload.

reuse_matrix.artifact: Model atoms; raw per-atom source slice/hash; source view/native coverage index
reuse_matrix.rebuild: New chunk span unions and per-record source metadata/provenance must be recomputed/revalidated.
reuse_matrix.reuse: Yes if complete source/atom/coordinate/version basis is unchanged. A boundary cut alone does not change them.

reuse_matrix.artifact: Raw leaf IDs, atom indices, leaf body text and own character spans
reuse_matrix.rebuild: owner_chunk_id, chunk_index, path/depth/parent and boundary metadata; saved source envelope must agree with new ownership.
reuse_matrix.reuse: Yes under fixed doc_id/atom basis/export mode. Legacy and source modes have distinct text contracts.

reuse_matrix.rebuild: Ordinal chunk ID/index may shift; prev/next edges and ownership joins must be regenerated. Never use chunk_id alone as cross-version text identity.
reuse_matrix.reuse: Possible for an unchanged span with same render mode.

reuse_matrix.artifact: Normalized leaf body and leaf token_est
reuse_matrix.rebuild: Inherited path/owner anchor can change. Carried token_est is not auto-recomputed when non-None, so stale caller-supplied estimates cannot be trusted as a new-budget result.
reuse_matrix.reuse: Normalized body is stable with same raw body+normalizer; text-only estimate is stable if recomputed consistently.

reuse_matrix.rebuild: Changed composed inputs require new encoding unless equality of effective token inputs is separately demonstrated. This audit did not tokenize or encode; differing strings are not proof that resulting vectors differ.
reuse_matrix.reuse: Only if the complete composed encoder string, encoder/tokenizer weights+revision, max length/truncation, pooling/normalization and numerical execution contract match. Exact composed-string equality is a conservative sufficient input gate.

reuse_matrix.rebuild: Changed split/merged chunk inputs need encoding; all affected vector-row/ID-map associations need remapping. Current builder rebuilds entire index.
reuse_matrix.reuse: Unchanged complete composed input under the same encoder contract can reuse a vector even when ID changes.

reuse_matrix.artifact: FAISS indexes and query-document pairwise scores
reuse_matrix.rebuild: Update index rows/maps for changed inputs; recompute global top-k/ranks if any competitor or mapping changes. Ties and numeric reproducibility were not executed here.
reuse_matrix.reuse: A whole index/hit result is reusable only if all vectors, membership, row/ID mapping and retrieval/query config are unchanged. An individual exact vector-query score may remain usable separately.

reuse_matrix.artifact: Anchor lexical features and BM25 scores
reuse_matrix.rebuild: Changed chunk corpus needs updated postings and corpus statistics. Stable leaf text does not freeze BM25 scores because N/df/avgdl may change.
reuse_matrix.reuse: Unchanged per-object composed anchor text may permit token/count reuse; owner-independent leaf lexical features can remain equal if path is unchanged.

reuse_matrix.artifact: Leaf hits to chunk candidates; RRF; tree adjacency
reuse_matrix.rebuild: Rerun owner joins, support sets/counts/max scores, RRF, chunk candidates and adjacency/expansion over new records.
reuse_matrix.reuse: No blanket reuse from leaf text or even identical hit lists.

reuse_matrix.artifact: Refiner atom encoder features versus retrieval leaf vectors
reuse_matrix.rebuild: Do not substitute them for retrieval vectors: retrieval consumes augmented strings and has its own truncation/normalization contract. No existing feature cache was inspected.
reuse_matrix.reuse: Same original atom encoder inputs/config/weights can conditionally reuse Refiner atom features.

verification.scope: Backend import isolation and builder wiring with fake encoder/index functions; no real numerical indexing.

witness_audit.method: Independent standard-library JSON/interval-set/literal-string reconstruction. No production modules imported or helpers executed; no tokenizer/model/API/ranking run.
review_boundaries: All 40 repository/protocol source hashes were mechanically rehashed; this is not a semantic review of every imported module.
Import/network denial and reported zero resources were reviewed in probe source and saved report, not independently re-executed by this reviewer.
The three import/wiring test passes were reported by root and not rerun or asserted as independent test evidence here.
Legacy exporter writes source=refiner_epoch8 even for this synthetic candidate; that constant is not evidence of an epoch8 model call.

Only default normalized exporter and four authored atoms are covered. No optional source_document mode, real retrieval candidates, budget selection, full HTTP request, source corpus or learned utility was tested.
Changed complete input does not prove changed vector/ranking/answer; identical tail encoder input does not make stale owner/ID mappings reusable.
